clue.text: Sally on leaving role has hit on tour

parts.note: a role in a play is a part

indicators.note: on tour things travel around, so these letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor gets a hit with a role while the show is travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name but is a witty remark; 'tour' sends the three words HAS HIT ON travelling into new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quip; the Parthian horsemen shot back while retreating, so the phrase names a cutting parting remark.

clue.text: Picture a stick-up by an armed horseman

parts.note: pic is short for picture

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word for stick is written bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A photo shows a hold-up committed by a mounted gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick-up' looks like a robbery, but 'up' reverses ROD to give DOR.
explanation.definitionFit: In a bullfight the mounted man who jabs the bull with a lance is this rider.

clue.text: Brief upset for hunter, say

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned over, so the word is written from the bottom up

parts.note: a hunter is a pocket watch with a cover, an example of a timer

explanation.surface: A short message overturned for someone who hunts.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter is a type of pocket watch, so a timer; 'upset' turns TIMER round.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is a set of instructions, which is what a remit is: an assigned area of responsibility.

clue.text: A halo, perhaps, that illumines us along the way?

definitions.text: A halo, perhaps, that illumines us along the way?

parts.words: A halo, perhaps, that illumines us along the way?
parts.note: a halo is literally a light round the head; the second reading is a lamp at the front of a car lighting the road

explanation.walkthrough: The saintly image of a halo is a playful split of a car lamp's name into head plus light.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's front lamp lights the road ahead as the vehicle travels.

clue.text: Distant note uplifting service

parts.note: A is a musical note

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up means the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A remote musical note lifts a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reverses RAF to FAR beneath A.
explanation.definitionFit: Far away and remote are synonyms for something at a great distance.

clue.text: Given a place for University after appeal is accepted in full

indicators.note: being accepted in means being taken inside, so these letters go within the word for full

parts.note: sated means full up

indicators.note: after places the university letter following the appeal word

parts.note: it is sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone is placed at a university once an appeal goes through completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' is sex appeal, a crossword convention; 'is accepted in' puts that and the university letter inside the word for full.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated has been located or set in a particular spot.

clue.text: Drive in spectacles, overlooking the speed

indicators.note: in a down clue overlooking means placed above the next part

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of glasses
mph (miles per hour) measures speed

explanation.surface: A driver in glasses ignores the speed limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' means energy, not motoring; the speed is the unit miles per hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is vigour or energetic force, which is what drive means here.

clue.text: Unwise to proceed without right forward

indicators.note: without means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: imprudent means unwise to act

explanation.surface: It is rash to go ahead without being in the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of cheeky or presumptuous matches insolent boldness.

clue.text: Unduly long expression of singular belief

parts.note: a creed is a set of beliefs

explanation.surface: A rambling statement of one person's faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, tedious piece of writing or speech.

clue.text: List containing order to flier of night fighter

indicators.note: containing means the tilt word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to list is to lean or tilt, as is to cant
OM is the Order of Merit
a bat flies at night

explanation.surface: A list includes an instruction to the pilot of a night fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' is the verb to lean, CANT; it holds OM and BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A combatant is a person engaged in fighting.

clue.text: Operatic heroine cold following take-off, say

indicators.note: following places the letter for cold after the heroine's name

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme

explanation.surface: A soprano catches a chill after her plane departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take-off' means an impersonation, not a plane leaving; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is an imitation, the kind of copying performance an impersonator gives.

clue.text: Remains in the keeping of churchwarden perhaps

definitions.text: Remains in the keeping of churchwarden perhaps

parts.words: Remains in the keeping of churchwarden perhaps
parts.note: a churchwarden is also a long clay tobacco pipe, and the remains are the unburnt plug left in its bowl

explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay pipe, not only a parish officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The half-smoked tobacco left in a pipe bowl has this name.

clue.text: Mother put out about husband's place in uproar

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the extinguishing word goes round the letter for husband

parts.note: to douse a fire is to put it out

explanation.surface: Mother extinguishes a fire near her husband's house in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaotic, noisy place is called this, from the old term for an asylum.

clue.text: State beset by storm damage

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the state goes inside the word for storm

parts.note: to rage is to storm
VA is Virginia, a US state

explanation.surface: A region battered by a storm suffers destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravage is to devastate or wreck.

clue.text: Tax haven for a top executive at last gets sanction

indicators.note: being a haven for something means sheltering it inside

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
a lid is a top

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of executive

explanation.surface: A tax shelter for a senior boss finally wins approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax haven' looks like a phrase, but VAT shelters A LID, then E ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to approve or confirm it officially.

clue.text: Favour brief letters to the point

indicators.note: letters here means the letters of brief are taken and rearranged

parts.note: the end is the point or tip

explanation.surface: A short letter asking a favour, getting straight to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters of 'brief' are rearranged, then the word for the point follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour someone by taking them up as a companion is to act as a friend to them.

clue.text: They obviously have to take care with horns that are crumpled

definitions.text: They obviously have to take care with horns that are crumpled

indicators.note: crumpled means squashed out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cattle farmers must be careful with bent-horned cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that are crumpled' rearranges CARE and HORNS; the whole clue describes cattle ranchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranch hands in the American West look after cattle, beasts that carry horns.

clue.text: Shrub causing ruminant distress if uprooted

parts.note: a camel chews the cud

indicators.note: in a down clue uprooted means pulled up, so the word runs bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to distress

explanation.surface: A bush makes a cud-chewing animal unhappy if dug up.
explanation.definitionFit: A camellia is a flowering evergreen bush.

clue.text: Armed units requiring first-class backing within patrolling limits

indicators.note: within means placed inside the rearranged letters
patrolling means moving around, so these letters are rearranged
backing means going backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: Soldiers need top support while patrolling the boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patrolling' means moving about, so 'limits' becomes MILITS; 'backing' turns the first-class mark round, and 'within' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Militias are bodies of citizen soldiers.

clue.text: Girl, we hear, apt to be out of place

indicators.note: we hear means the word for girl is taken by its sound

parts.note: Miss is a girl
fit means apt or suitable

explanation.surface: A girl apparently suited to being in the wrong place.
explanation.definitionFit: To misfit is to fit badly or be unsuited to one's surroundings.

clue.text: Joined forces in collective

explanation.definitionFit: People who joined forces came together, and those acting in a collective body are acting together as one.

clue.text: It posed a problem for a retainer

indicators.note: a problem suggests the letters are in a puzzle to be sorted into new order

explanation.surface: Something that caused a difficulty for a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retainer' looks like a servant but means an advance payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is an advance payment securing services, a type of down payment.

clue.text: Bit of a ladder revealed by party skirt

indicators.note: revealed by means coming next to, after the party word

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or game
a step is a rung of a ladder

explanation.surface: A ladder in a stocking shows through a party skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt' is the verb, to avoid; 'ladder' hints at tights but means the climbing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt an issue is to evade or dodge it.

clue.text: Shortly receiving money for a club

indicators.note: receiving means taking the money letter inside

parts.note: soon means shortly
P is a penny, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone will shortly get cash for joining a club.
explanation.walkthrough: A spoon is an old wooden golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a lofted wooden golf stick was called this.

clue.text: Call for bravery — but not when boxing?

definitions.text: Call for bravery — but not when boxing?

parts.words: Call for bravery — but not when boxing?
parts.note: the encouraging phrase urges courage, but literally lifting the jaw is bad advice for a boxer, who keeps it tucked

explanation.walkthrough: Boxers are taught to keep the jaw down, so the literal sense would be poor advice.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhortation to stay cheerful and brave in adversity.

clue.text: First person — or a nonentity

explanation.definitionFit: Number one is the person ranked first, and an unimportant person is dismissed as a nobody.

clue.text: Daughter supporting president in retirement

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed underneath

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president

explanation.surface: A daughter looks after a retired president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night means going to bed, so being in retirement means being in bed.

clue.text: Brief overture in quaint romance

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A short prelude to an old-fashioned love story.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction is a short opening section, which is what an overture is.

clue.text: Work in U.S.A. leading to debts liable to tax

indicators.note: leading to means coming first, before the debts

parts.note: labor is the American spelling of labour, work
IOUs are written promises of debt

explanation.surface: Work in America results in taxable debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax' is the verb, to strain, not a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laborious is taxing, demanding a great deal of effort.

clue.text: Old American pedigree is illuminating

parts.note: the Incan people were ancient Americans of Peru
descent is lineage or pedigree

explanation.surface: An ancient American lineage proves enlightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glowing white-hot gives off light, so it is shining.
